newsitem.title: USA: Wedding of a lifetime to cost far more in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Wedding of a lifetime to cost far more in 1997.

text.p: Love may be free, but it's getting progressively more expensive to tie the knot.

This year, the cost of holding the wedding of a lifetime costs far more than it did a year earlier. Two separate surveys show that overall increases for a formal wedding package range from 7.9 percent to more than 14 percent.

Getting married in style has never been more au courant, wedding experts say. As the 1997 wedding season gets under way, brides and grooms are holding elegant wedding receptions in record numbers, a distinct turnaround from the "less is more" attitude of the early 1990s.

Moet & Chandon Champagne, which tracks the cost of 12 key elements of an upscale June wedding in New York, said the Moet Matrimonial Matrix is showing the greatest percentage increase since the survey was started in 1994.
Prices this year rose an average of 7.9 percent. This follows a 3.6 percent rise in 1996, 4.8 percent increase in 1995 and a 0.8 percent rise in 1994, the first year the Matrix was published.
Blame it all on a robust economy.
"When Wall Street is up, as it is now, people are willing to spend more on their weddings," said Renny Reynolds, owner of Renny Floral and Party Design, a New York-based wedding and party planner.

Of 12 items, ranging from the wedding dress to the wedding license, seven items rose in price, two jumping more than 25 percent, Moet said. Nothing has gotten cheaper, but prices for four items were unchanged.

"This year, consumer willingness to spend on life's luxuries is clearly apparent in the wedding industry where demand is up for everything from food and champagne to flowers, dresses and venues," said Bernard Peillon, of Moet & Chandon.
The smallest price increase was for a 750 ml. bottle of Moet & Chandon Brut Imperial Champagne. It costs $35.50 now, up 4.6 percent from last year.
Invitations by Celebration Inc. rose 5.4 percent to $891 for 100 invitations.
Catering the wedding for 150 guests now costs $22,500, when provided by Great Performances Catering Inc. This is 7.1 percent higher than a year ago.
Cost of a rental tuxedo from Oscar de la Renta by Raffinati rose 10.5 percent to $105.
A photography package to document the happy day by Fred Marcus studio rose 10.6 percent to $3,125.
A seven night honeymoon package at the Ritz-Carlton in Kapalua, Hawaii, rose 25.4 percent to $3,155.
His and hers 18K gold wedding bands from H. Stern Jewellers showed the greatest percentage increase -- 31.7 percent to $790.

Costs of five of the 12 wedding essentials were unchanged. A classic wedding dress from Priscilla of Boston remained $1,780; bridal bouquet and groom's boutonniere by Renny Floral and Party Design was $375 and a wedding cake by Sylvia Weinstock Cakes Ltd. was $1,500.
A box of Hartz Mountain bird seed to shower the bride and groom, the ecologically-correct alternative to rice, remains $1.79.
Perhaps the biggest bargain, a City of New York wedding license, is $30. This price hasn't changed in seven years.
Modern Bride magazine puts the cost of a formal wedding with about 174 guests at $17,634, up 14.29 percent from $15,429 the year before.
The largest expense is the reception, costing $6,503, up from $5,157 the year before.
Another large jump is in the price of music, which costs now about $910, up from $747 a year earlier, the magazine said.
An engagement ring, now priced at about $2,909, rose from $2,536 and wedding rings for the couple, priced at $1,159, cost $1,034 a year earlier.

Don't think that you must be a June bride, Modern Bride says. Only 11.3 percent of weddings take place in June and the bridal market has new products and services for every month of the year. The magazine estimates that 2.34 million weddings will be held this year, for a total market value of over $35 billion.
This year, the fashion trend is to emulate the glamorous looks of Jackie Kennedy and Eva Peron, from dresses to jewelry.
This season, Modern Bride says, also look for the "Spanish" influence with full silhouettes in very ornate fabrics, especially heavily embroidered net and tulle.
White for brides is still No.1, but off-white and champagne are also popular. Colour only appears as an accent.
For the second year in a row, the popular wedding dress styles have dramatic backs with oversized details, such as bows and flowers.
For men, black is still the most traditional colour for a tuxedo, but navy and grey tones are gaining popularity.
